name: 20 Microns Limited
summary: 20 Microns Limited commits to sustainable procurement across its supply chain, integrating environmental, social, and governance criteria into sourcing decisions. The policy emphasizes responsible sourcing, supplier due diligence, human rights protection, and reducing environmental impacts such as emissions, waste, and resource consumption.
tagline: Sourcing responsibly for a sustainable future.

company.name: 20 Microns Limited
company.address: Waghodia – HO & RO, Delhi, Mumbai, Vadodara

declaration.preface: 20 Microns Limited has established a Sustainable Procurement Policy to guide responsible sourcing practices aligned with sustainability, ethical business operations, and compliance with applicable laws and international standards.
declaration.declaration: The company is committed to sustainable procurement practices that uphold ethical, environmental, and social standards across its supply chains, while promoting human rights, minimizing environmental impacts, and creating shared value.
declaration.scope: Applies to all procurement activities undertaken by 20 Microns Limited, including management, employees, customers, suppliers, contractors, workers, and other stakeholders working directly and indirectly for the company across offices, manufacturing plants, warehouses, and global procurement operations.

focusAreas: Supplier Due Diligence and Risk Assessment
Supply Chain Transparency and Community Benefits

Governance and Compliance: Embed sustainability principles into procurement guidelines
Ensure compliance with relevant laws and standards
Supplier Due Diligence: Evaluate adherence to labour, anti-corruption, and environmental requirements
Perform periodic supply chain risk assessments
Human Rights and Labour Protection: Address human rights risks for vulnerable groups
Prohibit forced labour, child labour, discrimination, harassment, and modern slavery
Respect freedom of association and collective bargaining
Environmental Stewardship: Reduce carbon emissions, waste generation, and resource consumption
Prevent deforestation, water pollution, and habitat destruction
Supply Chain Transparency and Capacity B: Provide sustainability training and supplier capacity building
Encourage suppliers to establish measurable sustainability objectives

quantitative.area: Supplier Code of Conduct and Sustainability Terms

targets.target: 100% of suppliers sign the code of conduct
100% of suppliers sign sustainability terms and conditions
100% of suppliers covered under sustainability assessment
40% of suppliers covered under on-site sustainability audits by number
70% of suppliers covered under on-site sustainability assessment by purchase volume
60% of suppliers covered in sustainability-related capacity building
100% of employees covered in sustainable procurement training on sustainable sourcing, energy efficiency, waste reduction and recycling
100% of employees covered in sustainable procurement training on labour rights, diversity and inclusion, community engagement, and health and safety
30% of suppliers with environmental certifications such as ISO 14001
30% of suppliers with labour and human rights certifications such as ISO 45001 and SA8000
100% of suppliers comply with environmental laws and regulations
100% of suppliers comply with labour and human rights laws and regulations

responsibilities.duty: Provides oversight and ensures alignment of the Sustainable Procurement Policy with the company’s overall sustainability strategy.
Implements the policy, conducts supplier due diligence, and monitors compliance with sustainability standards.
Adhere to the principles outlined in the policy and integrate them into their operations and supply chains.
Adhere to the sustainable procurement policy.

responsibilities.role: Lead Auditor – SAS, Head of SCM, Head of Purchase, Head of Sourcing
responsibilities.duty: Review the policy at least once every two years and update it when significant operational or business changes occur.

policy.monitoring: Compliance is monitored through regular audits, reviews, supplier sustainability assessments, on-site audits, KPI tracking, and periodic risk assessments. Monitoring frequency for KPIs is generally every 12 months.
policy.reviewMechanism: The policy is reviewed at least once every two years by the Lead Auditor – SAS, Head of Supply Chain Management (SCM), Head of Purchase, and Head of Sourcing, and may be updated earlier if significant changes occur in operations or business activities.
